problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,-1,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(-4,1,3)$ and $B(2,3,5).$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Straight Line
examples.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(\sqrt{2},0,-5)$ and is perpendicular to the line

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3 \\ y=-1+\sqrt{3}t \\ z=5-t.\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $\mathbf{q}=\langle \sqrt{2},0,-5 \rangle.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042677/assets/4c70e51d85874e5a241a5d9b35b147500d4c306187c5e0a1d15a48a9aef07706.png)

The direction vector of the line is $\mathbf{v}=\langle  0 , \sqrt{3} , -1\rangle,$ so a normal vector to the plane is 

$$
\mathbf{n}=\mathbf{v}=\langle  0 , \sqrt{3} , -1 \rangle.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,\sqrt{3},-1⟩ & =⟨\sqrt{2},0,-5⟩\cdot ⟨0,\sqrt{3},-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,\sqrt{3},-1⟩ & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,b,\,0⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨-1,1,-3⟩=8.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨-1,1,-3⟩=8$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-1,1,-3⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,1,-3⟩ & =0 \\ -{t}_{1}+{t}_{2}-3{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & ={t}_{1}+3{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{1}+3{t}_{3},{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the third component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{3}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{1}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{1}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{a}{b}=1.$
